summary: User-authorized termination placed stalled B/job 9715451 in EXIT; converged A/job 9715450 is accepted as the primary reactive C*+H* initial state and converged C/job 9715455 is retained as a far-separation reference.

payload.objective: Relax and compare three Fe(110) C*+H* coadsorption candidates for selecting the C* + H* -> CH* + * initial state.
current_evidence: B/job 9715451 was terminated under explicit user authority and LSF now reports EXIT. Its stopped non-converged outputs are preserved; no restart or resubmission occurred.

A/job 9715450 is a converged C-long-bridge + H-hollow coadsorption state with C-H 2.9728 A. C and H share local Fe38 coordination, the geometry audit passes, and its compatible TOTEN is -368.60093793 eV.
C/job 9715455 is a converged C-long-bridge + H-hollow far-separation state with C-H 4.5191 A, no shared local Fe coordination, a passing geometry audit, and compatible TOTEN -368.59979451 eV.
A is only 0.00114342 eV below C; they are near-degenerate but geometrically distinct relative-separation motifs.

A is selected as the primary reactive IS because it is the shorter, locally adjacent stable C*+H* state. C is retained as a far-separation reference because a direct C-to-CH path from C would mix long-range H surface migration into hydrogenation.
The accepted CH long-bridge product has the same cell, Fe45,C,H order, bottom-18 fixed mask, and C-H 1.1063 A, so A is structurally compatible for reviewed path construction.

If the user authorizes transition-state work, start a new transition-state-search task that uses A/job9715450 as IS, the accepted CH long-bridge structure as FS, and a chemically guided C-H-forming path with periodic-branch and geometry review before any NEB submission.
